WILDLIFE CONSERVATION & HABITAT MANAGEMENT IN SOUTH AFRICA: This course provides you with a unique understanding of the most up-to-date, in-field conservation techniques and practices, while exploring and contributing to important wildlife conservation work on the famous Hluhluwe-iMfolozi Park, known to be the birthplace of modern wildlife conservation in Africa. Course meetings will take place during the second eight weeks of the spring semester. Travel dates will be in May after the conclusion of the Spring 2027 semester. Course Description: Provides basic instruction on analyzing biological imaging data using statistical models and computer algorithms. Topics will include everything from basic data science and statistics to computer vision and analysis of histopathological, biomedical imaging, and remote sensing data. Previous experience with Python coding is recommended but not required Prerequisites: Stat 100, CPSC 440 or equivalent. This course will be located in the computer lab 607 IGB.

This course provides a basic foundation of different topics in genomics, including genome sequencing and annotation, gene mapping, genome prediction, gene expression analyses, inference of gene networks, and integration of multi-omics data. It also provides an overview of the benefits of genomics on agriculture and human health.

Students wishing to take the course should have introductory microbiology/molecular biology (e.g. MCB 100 or MCB 150) and introductory lab (e.g., MCB 101 or MCB 151) or equivalent course experience. Interested students may contact Dr. Crofts to discuss exceptions to these prerequisites. This course will be held in Animal Sciences Laboratory Room 322.

subject: ANSC
title: Bovine Assisted Reproductive Technologies
info: Prerequisite: ANSC 221 and ANSC 222 and ANSC 223 and ANSC 224 are required or equivalent.

sections.sectionText: The class will meet Wednesdays, March 24-May 5 with one 80-minute weekly virtual discussion. This is a 2-credit hour course with both online asynchronous and in-person synchronous components. Students will complete asynchronous lecture content online in addition to a synchronous in-person discussion meeting once per week on Wednesday from 9:00-10:20 AM. Off-campus students may join the discussion via Zoom. Students on campus are expected to attend in person. The course will cover reproductive technology and techniques utilized in cattle, including Bos taurus and Bos indicus. Topics include general bovine reproductive anatomy and physiology, estrus detection, estrous cycle control, estrus synchronization, pregnancy diagnosis, nutrition and disease concerns, collecting eggs and sperm, semen processing, in vitro and in vivo embryo production and emerging assisted reproductive technologies such as AI, IVF, MOET. The prerequisite for this course is ANSC 224.
